note: What makes each place feel lived in: an icon, live flavour lines (day and night), spots you can walk to, and signs. Spot x/z are metres from the place's centre (its x,y in places.csv). The SRC slates are fictional, use party-aligned colours only (no names, slogans or logos of real parties), get equal space, and none is the villain.

day: Someone is testing the mic: “Check, check, one-two.”
Vetkoek smell drifts across the paving.
Three SRC slates, three megaphones, one very patient security guard.
A jacaranda drops purple on the benches.
night: String lights on. Someone is freestyling on the stage.
Mam’ Gugu’s last kota goes for half price.
A guitar under the trees, and half the Quad singing along.

posters: Room to rent. R2500. Quiet. (It is not.)

day: The queue moves at the speed of the auntie’s ladle.
Bunny chow special: R35 and worth every cent.
Two people at the terrace arguing whether pap is breakfast.
night: Last orders. The chips are hot and the lights are humming.
Someone is studying over a cold plate of wors.

src_slates.name: Ubuntu Forward
lines: We fixed the bus shelter. Give us a year and we fix the bus.
Experience matters. So does the Wi-Fi password, and we have both.

src_slates.name: Free Food Fridays
lines: Free education, free Wi-Fi, free Fridays. Ask us how.
We are loud because the fees are louder.

src_slates.name: Fix-It Society
lines: We got the library printer working. Imagine what we do with your vote.
Clean audits, clean bathrooms. Boring? Maybe. Working? Yes.
